title: If as Special Form: Non-Strict Branch Evaluation
description: Adds if special form to evaluate. if evaluates test, then ONLY the chosen branch (yes or no). This avoids evaluating both branches like a regular function call would. Test: x=3; (if (< x 5) 100 200) -> 100; (if (= x 0) (/ 1 0) x) -> 3 (else branch taken, (/ 1 0) never evaluated, no error).

steps.description: tokenize and read same as before: tokenize splits, read recursively parses to AST.
PRIMITIVES dict with +, -, *, =, < as lambdas. symbols starts as copy.

evaluate: int returns itself. string looks up in symbols. define special form stores evaluated value. NEW: if special form at lines 38-40: unpacks test, yes, no; evaluates test; returns evaluate(yes) if truthy else evaluate(no). Only ONE branch evaluated. General call at lines 41-42 evaluates all parts then calls.
if is a special form: it controls which sub-expressions get evaluated. test evaluated first; based on result, exactly one of yes/no evaluated. This is non-strict (short-circuit) semantics.

steps.question: What does (if (= x 0) (/ 1 0) x) return when x=3, and why doesn't it error?
steps.answer: Returns 3. (= x 0) is false (3 != 0), so else branch x is evaluated. The then branch (/ 1 0) is NEVER evaluated because if is a special form that chooses only one branch. No division by zero error.

steps.description: run: tokenizes, loops reading and evaluating each form, prints non-None results.
Output: 100 (first if: 3 < 5 true -> 100), 3 (second if: 3 = 0 false -> else branch x=3). (/ 1 0) never runs.
